results.fact: Which way the variation leaves the standard line
results.correct_value: The standard North Face turns diagonally LEFT partway up pitch 2 (after the hueco wall); the Directisimo stays in the crack system and continues straight up it.
results.evidence: The standard North Face description says to stay left after the hueco wall, and that going right puts you on another line. A separate party commenting on the Directisimo says they got drawn into this crack after missing the standard route's diagonal left turn halfway up pitch 2; another says the topo follows the crack straight up. So the standard line steps LEFT and this variation goes straight/right up the crack — overview, pro_tips, pitch_detail[1] and rope_note wrongly said the standard line steps right.

results.fact: Descent rappel step location and nature
results.evidence: Retry found only more of the same: the standard description says the descent follows the climbing route (exposed class 3 with a few class 4 moves, SW ridge reached at a large notch via an easy gully); a 2025 solo report scrambled it at class 3 with no rappel; the WTA report used a different east-side line. No source places a rappel at a class-4 gully step at 7,600-7,700 ft, and the only rope-work account is the ~70-degree snow strand near the glacier-side notch. Would be settled by a second report locating the optional rappel.
No source found assigns a Grade II or III to the Southwest Ridge; all describe it only as class 3-4 and a 10-12 hr day. Would be settled by a guidebook commitment grade for this route.

The route listing gives '3200 ft (970 m), 3 pitches' (evidently the gain), and another route database gives 9 pitches and a 5,000 ft height — neither is a plausible technical length for a 3-pitch ridge and they disagree with each other. No source states the actual climbing length. Would be settled by a source giving the ridge's roped/technical length.

No source supports 5.8: the route database page grades the route 'III WI4' with no rock grade, and an archived description of the east-face route lists no rock grade either. Only one source gives the optional summit rock as 5.4 (the row's pitch_detail[4] agrees). 5.8 is likely borrowed from the South Buttress. Would be settled by a second source grading the summit rock pitches, or an owner decision to clear rock_grade.
